purpose: Persistent lifecycle contract for canonical knowledge claims. Research claims inside run-scoped evidence databases are not canonical claims.

field_semantics.claim_id: Stable canonical claim identifier assigned when a claim enters the persistent knowledge layer.
field_semantics.knowledge_id: Stable ID of the canonical document or knowledge object that owns this claim.
field_semantics.knowledge_type: Temporal knowledge type inherited from the owning canonical knowledge object.
field_semantics.text: Canonical factual proposition. Material factual changes create a new canonical claim rather than silently rewriting this text.
field_semantics.topic: Research or knowledge topic used for retrieval and review grouping.
field_semantics.status: Current lifecycle state of the canonical claim.
field_semantics.created_at: Project-timezone date when this canonical claim was first created.
field_semantics.as_of: Real-world date through which the claim is intended to describe reality.
field_semantics.last_verified_at: Most recent date on which the canonical claim was substantively revalidated.
field_semantics.next_review_at: Date on which an active claim becomes due for freshness review.
field_semantics.relations: Explicit lifecycle relationships to other canonical claims.
field_semantics.provenance: Audit trail linking the canonical claim to research evidence or a documented manual basis.

rules: Run-scoped research claims and persistent canonical claims are different object classes.
A research claim does not become canonical merely because supporting evidence exists.
Canonical promotion requires an explicit human-controlled promotion step.
Canonical claim text is not silently rewritten when reality changes; create a new claim and relate it using supersedes when appropriate.
A contradicted claim remains in history and is not deleted.
A superseded claim remains queryable as historical knowledge.
Document-level active status does not imply every canonical claim is active.
Claim-level lifecycle changes must preserve provenance and history.
Templates, drafts, and unpromoted research output do not create canonical claims.
No automated agent may mark a canonical claim active without a defined review or promotion gate.
The Git-tracked canonical claim ledger is the authoritative persistent history.
The runtime SQLite canonical claim index is derived state and may be deleted and rebuilt.
Lifecycle history must not depend solely on mutable SQLite rows.

storage_semantics.runtime_index: SQLite materialized view rebuilt from ledger
